I want to be able to tell them by EOD Friday whether we can offer a non-binding hold and what the fallback options are. Attaching the Orbis estimate for reference.

Thanks —
Alex

> Team —

> OrbisAI is at verbal on the Q3 Dedicated commit (referenced in HubSpot DEAL-2029-0784). They shared a new load estimate this morning (attached). Before I confirm a soft allocation, can we run a quick internal availability sweep and a conservative sizing check? Key asks:
>

> - What is the realistic SLA-backed throughput (tokens/sec) per slot for their estimated mixed-batch profile?
> - Any conflicts with existing Reserved / Dedicated commitments in the us-west region for that timeframe?

Quick preliminary answers below — I can hand this off to Ops for a full readout if we want to push a temporary hold.

1) Availability: We have ~120 p100-equivalent throughput available in us-west across Dedicated fleets today. However, 45 of those are already earmarked for committed contracts with Q3 start dates that haven't been fully provisioned in our capacity system. Practically speaking, we can carve ~40 slots as a soft allocation if we accept two caveats:
  - We label it a "soft hold" (no contractual capacity reservation) until finance signs off on a commit or we move to a reserved capacity SKU.
  - We may need to schedule orchestration to ensure those slots are not auto-allocated for burst traffic in early July.

2) Throughput per slot: For Orbis' mixed batch profile (their CSV suggests 60% short chat + 40% long-form inference), realistic median throughput for p100-eq is ~1,900 tokens/sec per slot when configured with continuous batching and KV-cache disabled for long-form bursts. If they want consistent 99th pct latency, we'd land closer to ~1,200 tokens/sec and should recommend a hybrid profile (some higher-memory variants pinned).

3) Conflicts: No maintenance windows currently scheduled against that mid-July to Sept window. The risk is new commitments from inbound enterprise deals we expect to close in April-May (TBD).

I can produce a 30/60/90 projection and a short ops handoff doc by EOD today. If Marissa can confirm the node mapping and any previously promised soft allocations, we can propose language for a soft-hold to Orbis.

-Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OrbisAI Q3 sizing — quick availability sweep request

Alex / Karthik —

I pulled the fleet outlook and attached a short snapshot (redwood_gpu_snapshot_20290403.pdf). Highlights:

- Us-west Dedicated pool: nominal capacity 320 p100-eq. Current committed baseline for Q3 (known contracts) = 245 p100-eq. That leaves a nominal buffer of ~75 p100-eq.
- Of the 75 buffer, ~18 p100-eq is earmarked as "standby" for high-priority partners (internal note) but not contractually reserved.
- We have 7 nodes scheduled for kernel upgrades the week of 2029-07-15; those upgrades reduce peak throughput by ~8 p100-eq for 48 hours each.
- If we accept a soft allocation for Orbis (40 p100-eq), we should:
   1) Mark an internal ticket to prevent auto-burst allocation for those hours (ops action).
   2) Offer a fallback plan (if needed) to route overflow to us-east with a 5–10% latency penalty and explicit cost uplift.

Recommendation: Offer Orbis a 21-day soft allocation window (non-binding) that converts to a reserved capacity SKU upon signed commit. This reduces risk of double-booking and buys us time to finalize billing/legal.

I can push the ops ticket today once Alex confirms we'd like to present the soft-hold language.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.ai

Subject: OrbisAI Q3 Dedicated sizing — proposal for soft allocation and next steps

Sara —

Thanks again for sending the updated Q3 load. Quick internal check shows we can offer a non-binding soft allocation for the volume you outlined (circa 40 p100-equivalent slots) for the mid-July through September window. A few clarifying points and next steps:

- What we can offer now: a 21-day soft allocation (no upfront payment, not reflected in contractual reserved capacity) that prevents your expected slots from being auto-allocated for burst customers. This gives you a window to finalize procurement and for us to convert to a reserved SKU if you decide to commit.
- Performance: conservative 99th pct throughput estimate is ~1,200 tokens/sec per p100-eq slot for your mixed profile. We'll supply a hybrid mapping that includes a small percentage of higher-memory variants to keep long-form latency consistent.
- Ops caveat: there are scheduled kernel upgrades the week of July 15 that may reduce peak capacity for a short window; we'll coordinate a maintenance blackout or schedule migration around your peak if needed.
- Next steps I propose:
  1) Orbis confirms you'd like a 21-day soft allocation hold.
  2) We'll open an internal ops ticket and send you a soft-allocation acknowledgment (non-binding) with the fallback routing plan to us-east.
  3) Procurement shares expected contract timeline (approx signing date).

If you want, we can do a 30-minute tech check with Marissa this week to validate the throughput numbers against a small synthetic workload.

Best —
Alex Martinez
